title: Playing multiple funerals a day and pay
summary: Dejan explains how three funerals in a day were possible because Catholic funerals were short, while Baptist ones ran for hours. He recalls the pay of a dollar and a half a round, long processions past the deceased's bar, and charging double for two-way parades.

blocks.x: You know, when you were talking to me over the phone you said sometimes you play three funerals in one day.
I have a hard time believing that because I used to remember funerals that would last about four hours. Oh, some funerals would last five or six hours.

It would last four hours. I don't see how you could play three in one day. Yeah. You see, the Catholic funerals never last long. Oh. You see, if you get two Catholic funerals in the morning and one o'clock, maybe one, two o'clock, you're playing a Baptist or Protestant funeral, well you'd probably be in the street until six, seven o'clock. But you get through them Catholic funerals in no time. Now sometimes you catch a Baptist funeral that the fellow never belonged to no church and they dismiss them right from the house. Well now they really have the funeral procession at the church at night and they just dismiss the next day. But one time if a fellow didn't belong to no church or nothing and the preacher didn't want to do no lying about him or nothing, they just would dismiss him from the house, you know. And so sometimes you catch a Catholic, a Baptist, and maybe two Baptists, you see. Yeah, I played three a day already. And two a day was common. But you see it all the time, I go for that little dollar and a half, two rounds, and then if you went to three dollars, you're making three dollars of man, you were raising hell. So we'd live from Al Jays to Walkatown, man. And then on the way of coming back, you'd play a parade. Yeah, stop that. I stopped that. You know, I told them, I said, no, one way. Two ways, I charge them double price, that's all. Yeah, but man, one time they had to pass the man in front of his door. And bar him where he used to bump, might be six blocks away, had to go pass in front of that bar room. Then you had to go to the graveyard, if the graveyard was walking distance, sometimes you had to turn them loose before you hit the graveyard. Then coming back, they're making a parade all around where he used to bump at and all like that. Four or five hours wasn't nothing for a funeral one time. Yeah, I played them.
